text.p: Bonds lost in line with other European markets as first round voting in French elections raised the possibility of conservative President Jacques Chirac having to share power with a Socialist-led government.
The spread with the 10-year cash bunds was seen widening but support should remain firm at the shorter end of the curve, leading it to steepen, traders said.

The spread with the 10-year Spanish Bono was widening slightly to a negative 17 basis points from 14 at Friday's close. Chartists saw support for the futures contract, which was losing 37 basis points at 108.78, at around 108.50.
"The market was not expecting a left-wing victory," said one trader referring to the French election first round vote.
"Even if it is the second round that really counts, there is a temptation to sell, especially at the longer end," he added.
Dealers said that the slight weakness of the escudo, following the international trend, should not unsettle the shorter end of the curve.
